newsitem.title: DENMARK: Rieber mulls new Phoenix bid.
newsitem.headline: Rieber mulls new Phoenix bid.

text.p: Norway's Rieber & Son said on Wednesday that it might raise its bid for Danish roadbuilder Phoenix Contractors before Friday's deadline for a new Rieber offer expires.
"We continue to mull the possibility of raising our offer but the management has not decided when it will make any announcement," Rieber managing director Olav Daviknes told Reuters.
Rieber's hitherto favoured bid of 820 million Danish crowns was trumped on Saturday by latecomer Icopal's offer of 875.8 million crowns.

Another suitor, major Danish construction and chemicals group Superfos, has said it will not raise its offer of 808 million crowns but nevertheless considers itself still in the race. It shares with Rieber a March 7 bid-expiry deadline.
Superfos, the only bidder from among the Copenhagen Stock Exchange's top 20 listed companies, is favoured by the pension funds which are Phoenix's largest shareholders.
A 776 million crown bid by yet another suitor, building contractor Marius Pedersen, expired last week.
When Icopal last Friday said it would make an eleventh-hour bid, Phoenix said that the plan was hostile and unhelpful.
Following Saturday's disclosure of the size of Icopal's bid however, Phoenix said it would make no further substantive comment on the battle.
Rieber on Wednesday said that if defeated in its pursuit of Phoenix it would seek other ways into the Danish asphalt market.
"If we fail to take over Phoenix we shall consider other plans we have ready," Daviknes said, refusing to elaborate.

With 17.1 percent of Phoenix equity and 19.2 percent of voting stock, Rieber said it had yet to decide whether to raise its bid or sell its holding but would not retain its current position to block other suitors.

The most-traded Phoenix C-share stood on Wednesday afternoon at 710 crowns, 10 crowns down from Tuesday's close. Rieber was unchanged at 225 Norwegian crowns, Superfos was up two crowns to 787 and Icopal slipped 30 crowns to 1,550. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
